summary: Montefiore notified twelve Bronx utilization-review nurses that their positions would be eliminated. The nurses reviewed patient charts and worked with insurers over coverage; NYSNA alleges that Datavant AI-assisted software took over work that required clinical judgment and that Montefiore failed to meet with the union under negotiated staffing and technology safeguards. The union filed a grievance and later said the layoffs took effect in early September, while July reporting described a July 12 effective date; that chronology is not reconciled here. Montefiore called the union account inaccurate and misleading and described a nonclinical paperwork program, without publicly supplying a case-specific technical workflow or grievance resolution. No patient denial, data breach or final contractual breach is established.

assessment_boundaries: The incorporated technology tentative agreement and complete grievance/response are not publicly reconstructed here; the conditional route and its applicability remain contested.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: NYSNA originally announced the proposed elimination of twelve utilization-review nurses and alleges Datavant software replacement. Bloomberg Law reports a filed grievance asserting that notices preceded a required meeting about alternatives and that a technology clause called for talks if AI reduced staffing. An affected nurse later described her own work and the software use; NYSNA’s September 4 bulletin says layoffs took effect that week. July reporting said the layoffs took effect July 12, leaving timing unreconciled. The publicly linked 2026 mediator memorandum incorporates separate tentative agreements but does not reproduce the technology text, so it corroborates a new contract but not the exact AI trigger. Montefiore denies the replacement characterisation and describes nonclinical paperwork changes. The union’s account is first-party allegation, not a finding of contract breach; patient and privacy risks remain prospective, with no documented patient-level consequence. A later National Nurses United publication says Marilyn Shuler lost her utilisation-review position and moved to case management. This establishes reported reassignment of one worker, not the income or employment outcome for all twelve. The full originating article was retrieved during the withdrawal audit. The full September 28 NNU article also reports that Laurel Carlin-Leclerc was forced to retire early and that the former home-working role allowed her to oversee care for her sick husband. The article gave nurses 45 days to find other positions; it does not establish twelve cases of unemployment or wage loss.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The potential governance failure is an avoided negotiated consultation route if AI-caused staffing reduction triggered it. The public evidence establishes a grievance and displaced roles, but not the complete operative clause, agreed scope or resolution of whether that conditional trigger occurred. It does not establish an automated clinical decision or patient injury. The alleged negotiated meeting route remains conditional on the operative clause and AI-causation trigger, both disputed. The unresolved contractual duty has no matching admitted canonical requirement; it is not replaced with a generic standards duty. Workforce loss does not establish automated clinical authority or patient harm, and the conflicting effective dates remain bounded. The independent labour-rights assessment is Boundary. The operative consultation condition and its trigger remain disputed. Displaced positions remain documented. Reassignment mitigates one worker’s employment outcome. The separately reported forced early retirement supports material but bounded livelihood loss without a monetary estimate. Patient harms remain prospective and the consultation trigger remains disputed.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This case tests how a conditional workforce consultation safeguard is evidenced when the employer and union dispute the AI system’s role. Preserving the grievance, contract incorporation and later layoff report makes the governance question concrete without treating the union’s allegation as an adjudicated bypass.

NYSNA reports that twelve utilisation-review positions were eliminated and layoffs took effect. The September 28 first-party NNU report describes a 45-day period to find other positions, Shuler’s loss of her role and reassignment to case management, and Carlin-Leclerc being forced to retire early; her former home-working role enabled care for her sick husband. This supports actual, material but bounded occupational/livelihood loss under the alternative S3 criterion where no defensible USD valuation is available. S2 alone understates the forced premature exit from a long-standing nursing role; S4 solvency or widespread economic impact is not established. Reassignment does not establish wage loss for Shuler or outcomes for all twelve, but it cannot negate the independently reported early retirement and completed displacement. The union’s AI-substitution account remains attributed and employer-disputed; patient injury, pension loss and a legal breach are not inferred.
